coverage_note: State and local public employees generally, under Tex. Gov't Code chapter 617, which bars public officials from recognizing or contracting with a labor organization. Firefighters and police officers in political subdivisions that adopt Tex. Local Gov't Code chapter 174 by local election, and the meet-and-confer arrangements in Local Gov't Code chapters 142, 143 and 146, are exceptions not covered cell by cell here.

governing_statute.value: Tex. Gov't Code chapter 617 (Collective Bargaining and Strikes): public-sector collective bargaining is prohibited
governing_statute.quote: (a) An official of the state or of a political subdivision of the state may not enter into a collective bargaining contract with a labor organization regarding wages, hours, or conditions of employment of public employees. (b) A contract entered into in violation of Subsection (a) is void.

labor_board.null_reason: Texas prohibits public-sector bargaining for covered employees and no statute captured creates a public-sector labor relations board.

ulp_limitation_period.null_reason: No public-sector unfair labor practice procedure exists in the Texas statutes captured for this row.

who_may_bargain.value: No public employee under general law; officials may not recognize a labor organization as bargaining agent. Firefighters and police officers may bargain where the political subdivision adopts Local Gov't Code chapter 174 by election.
who_may_bargain.quote: (c) An official of the state or of a political subdivision of the state may not recognize a labor organization as the bargaining agent for a group of public employees.

scope_of_bargaining.null_reason: No bargaining is permitted under Gov't Code chapter 617, so there is no statutory scope for covered employees; public employees keep the right to present grievances individually or through a representative that does not claim the right to strike (617.005).

impasse_procedure.null_reason: No bargaining, so no impasse procedure, for covered Texas public employees. Chapter 174 provides arbitration boards for firefighters and police in adopting jurisdictions (Local Gov't Code 174.153), outside this row's coverage.

strike_legality.value: Prohibited; a striking public employee forfeits civil service, reemployment and other public-employment rights
strike_legality.quote: (a) Public employees may not strike or engage in an organized work stoppage against the state or a political subdivision of the state. (b) A public employee who violates Subsection (a) forfeits all civil service rights, reemployment rights, and any other rights, benefits, and privileges the employee enjoys as a result of public employment or former public employment.

agency_fee_status.value: Prohibited. Texas bars denying public employment for membership or nonmembership in a labor organization, and Janus v. AFSCME (2018) bars agency fees from nonconsenting public employees.
agency_fee_status.quote: An individual may not be denied public employment because of the individual's membership or nonmembership in a labor organization.
